key_insight: Deep Interaction proposes a more efficient way for humans to correct large reasoning models by targeting the exact faulty step instead of re-running the whole reasoning process. This aims to reduce repeated mistakes and make human-AI collaboration more reliable.
problem_solved: Current human-AI interaction for chain-of-thought reasoning is inefficient: when a model makes an error, users often need to regenerate answers or repeatedly point out mistakes, but the model may still produce similar errors. The paper addresses the need for precise, step-level correction in long reasoning tasks.
method: Introduces an interaction method designed to let users pinpoint and correct specific reasoning steps.
Focuses on improving efficiency compared with full regeneration or broad follow-up prompting.
Aims to reduce repeated error loops by making corrections more local and actionable.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this could make debugging and steering large reasoning models much faster and more dependable. It is especially useful in workflows where correctness matters and iterative prompting is too slow or error-prone.

paper_title: Deep Interaction: An Efficient Human-AI Interaction Method for Large Reasoning Models
paper_authors: Hefeng Zhou, Jinxuan Zhang, Jiong Lou, Yuxin Liu, Chaochao Lu
